title: Landing headline flavors and routing playbook
content:
Overview and goals:

This doc is a working playbook for a set of headline/tagline and early fold microcopy experiments for the homepage and product landing pages. Objective: validate which positioning is clearest and highest converting for mid-market engineers and platform teams who are comparing managed inference options vs DIY on infra. Secondary objective: capture messaging that scales across Dedicated and Private offerings while keeping Hosted as the fastest path to value.

Audience breakouts (prioritized):
- Platform engineers at scale-ups (priority): care about predictable throughput, cost per token, and operational controls (autoscale, fallbacks, rollouts).
- ML/infra engineers at mid-market/enterprise: want model portability, private deployments, and deterministic SLOs for latency and reliability.
- Product engineers / PMs (lower touch): want low-friction integration and clear ROI hooks.

Top-level positioning hypotheses to test (each mapped to headline + subhead):
1) Predictable inference economics: "Pay for inference you can plan for"
   - Subhead candidates: "Committed capacity, transparent per-token economics, and tools to tune throughput without surprise bills."
   - Rationale: Targets procurement and infra teams who fear black-box usage spikes.

2) Unified serving across environments: "One API to run models everywhere"
   - Subhead candidates: "Hosted, dedicated, or private — same API, same rollouts, same observability."
   - Rationale: Differentiates from single-mode vendors and DIY stacks.

3) Production-grade reliability & graceful degradation: "Keep apps online even when models fail"
   - Subhead candidates: "Automatic fallbacks, canary deploys, and per-route SLAs that prevent outages."
   - Rationale: Targets teams for whom service continuity matters more than squeeze-out cost optimizations.

4) Developer speed + predictable performance: "Ship LLM features — without building an ops team"
   - Subhead candidates: "SDKs, quickstart templates, and performance profiles verified for real workloads."
   - Rationale: PLG-oriented hook for quick adoption.

Competitive callouts (quick notes to weave into microcopy where relevant):
- Major managed LLM APIs lean on model access and simplicity; highlight our cost transparency and routing primitives as points of differentiation. Avoid direct comparison to brand names, instead emphasize "vendor lock-in risk" vs "portable API."
- Inference infra vendors (self-hosted runtimes) sell control; our framing: "control without ownership" — show examples of when Dedicated + Private are preferable and how they map to procurement cycles.
- Cloud provider endpoints: emphasize predictable SLAs and multi-region routing rather than low-level infra specs.

Experiment matrix (high-level):
- Metric suite: homepage CTR to signup, product page click-through to pricing, trial activation rate, and time-to-first-successful-inference (tracked by onboarding funnel). Ongoing: retention by feature (rollouts, canary, cost dashboard) at 30/90 day.
- Variants (A/B/N): run parallel headline groups (Hypotheses 1–4) for 2 weeks with balanced traffic; rotate secondary microcopy and CTA wording.
- Secondary microcopy: test mention of "per-token transparency" vs "reserved capacity" in the hero subhead.

Hero copy variants (short list of fresh lines to use directly in tests):
- Headline A: "Inference that behaves like you expect"
  - Sub: "Predictable cost, predictable latency — across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments."
  - CTA: "Start a predictable trial"

- Headline B: "Run models without building a whole stack"
  - Sub: "Unified API, verified perf profiles, and operational controls for production apps."
  - CTA: "Try our quickstart (5 mins)"

- Headline C: "Make serving decisions, not servers"
  - Sub: "Routing, fallback, and capacity policies that keep LLM features fast and affordable."
  - CTA: "See economics in your workload"

- Headline D: "Ship LLM features with SLOs you can trust"
  - Sub: "Canary rollouts, traceable latency budgets, and built-in fallbacks."
  - CTA: "Explore SLAs and rollouts"

Microcopy and supporting lines for product pages:
- Feature blurbs (short):
  - Serving runtime: "GPU-optimized kernels, continuous batching, and KV cache tuning for real user traffic."
  - Routing: "Route by latency, cost, or region with automated fallback policies."
  - Observability: "Trace tokens from request to cost with per-route dashboards and exportable traces."
  - Optimize: "Actionable batch and quantization tips tailored to your usage patterns."

- Pricing teases: "Transparent per-token pricing with reserved capacity options for predictable spend."

SEO and organic framing suggestions (for near-fold content and H2s):
- H2 candidates: "Inference pricing explained", "How to choose hosted vs dedicated vs private", "Latency SLOs for LLMs: what matters"
- Long-tail keyword phrases to insert naturally: "inference cost optimization", "LLM serving for production", "private LLM deployment guide"

Wireframe copy routing rules (how to decide which microcopy to show):
- New visitor (unknown company size): show Hypothesis 2 heading (one API) + developer speed CTA.
- Known mid-market or enterprise IP (via IP lookup, cookie or prior funnel data): show Hypothesis 1 or 4 (economics or SLOs) with a secondary link to Dedicated/Private overview.
- Returning developer who visited docs: show Hypothesis 3 (reliability) and a prompt to "Compare plans" linking to reserved capacity examples.

Acceptance criteria for headline winner (to promote to root hero):
- Stat lift: statistically significant improvement in CTR to product page and 15% higher trial activation vs baseline over 2 weeks and 10k+ visitors.
- Qualitative: support tickets from trialers mentioning clarity of pricing or routing at a lower rate than baseline (proxy for confusion).

Open questions and research needs (action items):
- Get engineering to provide 2–3 concrete mini-case numbers showing latency and cost improvements for a sample workload (chat, 2k tokens) for use in subhead and bullets. Owner: Diego. Due: 2025-01-20.
- Confirm legal's rules for comparative language (owner: Maya).
- Run quick customer interview script with 6 platform engineers to surface wording that resonates around "control" vs "ownership" (owner: Liam).

Quick snippets for social/blog headlines (spin-offs once hero chosen):
- "Why predictable inference beats surprise bills"
- "From prototype to 100M tokens: serving patterns that scale"
- "One API, three deployment modes: pick what you need, keep the same code"

Appendix: sample 2-line test email subject for trial drives:
- Subject A: "Try predictable inference: reserved capacity, simple pricing"
- Subject B: "Ship your LLM feature — no infra build required"

Notes on tone and voice: favor concise engineering-forward language; avoid marketing hyperbole. Use concrete verbs (route, pin, reserve, rollback) rather than adjectives. Keep CTAs action-oriented and specific ("Start a reserved trial" beats "Learn more").

End of draft. Follow-ups: convert top 2 headline winners into hero designs for the next design sprint, and schedule A/B traffic allocation with Growth for the second week post-launch.
